html:
Tobacco has been Malawi's main export for most of the time since colonial rule, and the country is one of the world's largest growers of burley tobacco.

Settlers began growing it in the Shire Highlands in the 1890s, and African tenants and smallholders soon grew it too, often on estates under harsh terms. After independence Banda and his allies built large estates, and from the 1990s smallholders were allowed to grow burley freely.

Tobacco sold at the auction floors of Lilongwe has made up a large share of export earnings, so falling world demand from anti-smoking campaigns hurts the whole economy of Malawi. It shaped the farming of Nyasaland too.
sum: Tobacco has been Malawi's main export for most of the time since colonial rule, and the country is one of the world's largest growers of burley tobacco.
